messages:
maria_ml: Quick heads-up — ran a small bring-up for the new 11B candidate (codename: conductor) quantized to int6 on our smoke slices. Need a quick cost vs quality read before we propose routing flags.

jin_eng: Awesome, can you drop the key numbers? latency / p95 / tokens/sec and any regression signals?

maria_ml: TL;DR: throughput up ~2.6x vs 11B-int8 baseline, avg token latency down ~28%. Cost per 1M tokens ~ $42 (int6) vs $110 (int8) on the same fleet. Quality: small drop on multi-turn E2E QA EM: -1.8% absolute, factuality metric -2.2 points on our 5k smoke set.

sam_sre: Numbers look promising for throughput. Did you see any increased tail latency or OOMs with kv cache?

maria_ml: No OOMs on our standard mem config. p99 latency increased slightly for very long contexts (>2k tokens) — p99 +12%. That aligns with more cache thrash on int6 kernels; we saw spikes in kvcache misses.

oliver_prod: From product POV — what's the user-visible impact of the -1.8% EM? any systematic failure modes (e.g., more hallucinations, fewer concise answers)?

maria_ml: Good question. Quick qualitative pass: more verbosity and a few extra low-confidence hallucinations on knowledge cutoff probes. Short, deterministic completions (templated replies) are unaffected. We logged examples in the binder: /mnt/eval/threads/conductor_int6_examples.log

natalie_gtn: For GTN, this is promising if we can preserve SLAs for high-value routes. Proposal: hybrid routing — int6 for fast/default, int8 for verified intents (payments, legal, search rerank). Can we simulate split traffic economics?

maria_ml: Ran a quick sim: 70% traffic int6 + 30% int8 yields ~1.9x cost reduction vs full int8 and keeps EM drop to ~0.6% on weighted slice (because critical slices remain int8). If we route 90/10 it's ~2.4x cost reduction but EM hit ~1.2%.

jin_eng: Can we sketch a canary plan? Minimal config we can ship to Redwood Dedicated and Hosted to measure production-slice regressions safely?

maria_ml: Canary plan I suggest:
1) 2% global traffic: conductor-int6
2) 4x traffic sampling of critical slices (payments, auth, search) routed to int8 to compare side-by-side
3) 24h automatic rollback if factuality score drops >1.5 points on those critical slices or latency p95 increases >30%

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary created: conductor-int6 @ 2% traffic. Monitoring hooks: latency, kvcache-misses, factuality-score.

sam_sre: Add one more guard: circuit-breaker on p99 > 1.5s for 5m window. Also enable heap metrics alert—int6 kernels behave differently.

oliver_prod: Product OK with the 2% canary + hybrid gating. We also want a short UX QA pass (2 PMs) on conversational prompts to watch tone and hallucination.

maria_ml: Will do. I'll add a short eval run with ~2k multi-turn dialogues and collect qualitative diffs. Next steps: finalize routing config snippet (will paste here), start 2% canary, and iterate after 24h metrics.

jin_eng: Routing config snippet (suggested):
```json
{
  "route": "/api/generate",
  "variants": [
    {"model": "conductor-11b-int6", "weight": 0.02},
    {"model": "conductor-11b-int8", "weight": 0.98, "selectors": ["critical" ]}
  ],
  "fallback": "conductor-11b-int8",
  "guards": {"p99_latency_ms": 1500, "factuality_drop_points": 1.5}
}
```

natalie_gtn: Perfect. Once we have 24h metrics, we'll decide an initial split (70/30 vs 90/10) for a ramp.

maria_ml: Recording follow-ups: I'll push the eval bundle and example failures to the binder, tag @oliver_prod and @natalie_gtn for UX/GTN review, and keep SRE looped for alerts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
